item.title: Check Out the Final Columbus Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan Report
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Check Out the Final Columbus Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan Report

The Columbus Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan (ACIP) report is now available for your review! Read the finalized plan. Community engagement throughout this process was crucial, and you shared a lot of valuable input with 10 community meetings and 2,400 survey respondents. Your feedback helped the department design two pools that opened this summer, as well as two pools that will be replaced in the near future. These new pools will fit the needs of Columbus residents and programming for years to come. Read more about the pools that opened this summer below. Columbus Recreation and Parks Department is also currently in the initial planning stages for a new indoor aquatics center so stay tuned for more updates!

 

Visit the New Windsor Pool

The brand-new Windsor Pool, located at 1300 Windsor Ave., is now open to the public! This pool includes a lot of great features, such as dual water slides, a dedicated diving pool, an eight-lane lap pool, a kiddie pool with lots of bubblers and spray features for younger kids to enjoy, an upgraded pool house and sheltered and shaded recreation areas.

 

Explore the New Glenwood Pool

This summer, the newly-renovated Glenwood Pool, located at 1888 Fairmont Ave., was also completed! This brand-new outdoor pool features dual water slides, a dedicated diving pool, a six-lane lap pool, a kiddie pool, an upgraded pool house and sheltered and shaded recreation areas.

 

To visit a Columbus Recreation and Parks Department pool, get a Leisure Card for free at your local community center. Admission is only $1 per person. Swing by to explore these brand-new pools before the summer’s over! Learn more about the department's pools.

item.description:

Last Chance to Comment on the Initial Aquatics Design Concepts! 

Last day to comment: 
Friday, Jan. 14

Do you care about Columbus’ indoor pool, outdoor pools and spray parks? Do you want to see Columbus add more aquatics facilities? Then don’t forget to review the initial aquatics design concepts! Through the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan, residents shared their suggestions and ideas from filling out the online survey, participating in Zoom meetings and sharing on-site feedback at the pools last summer, which developed into these initial design concepts.

Review these concepts and provide feedback on any or all of the initial designs here: www.columbusaquatics.org/commentform. These concepts are preliminary only, and your comments will help prioritize what is included in the final designs. All comments are due by this Friday, Jan. 14!

  • Want to learn more about the sites and designs for each concept? Watch the virtual meeting video recording.
  • Ready to add your feedback? Share your comments about the proposed initial aquatics design concepts.

Thank you to everyone who has already shared your comments! Public outreach has been a huge part of the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan, and this process would be impossible without hearing what you want in your aquatics facilities in Columbus. Thank you for your feedback during this process!

Learn more about the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan at www.columbusaquatics.org.

item.title: Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan Survey is Now Available
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan Survey
is Now Available

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department currently manages eight outdoor pools and one indoor pool at the Columbus Aquatics Center, as well as seven spray parks and fountains, which are great ways for small kids to cool off in the summer heat. There are diverse programs offered all over the city of Columbus – some of which you may have already taken part in!

To make sure these facilities meet the needs of residents, we are kicking off the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan to learn what you need and want to see in our aquatics facilities and programs!

All residents are asked to fill out a short online survey through Saturday, May 15, sharing their thoughts about the current aquatics facilities. Fill out the survey here.

Additionally, our department will be having an online public meeting via Zoom to get feedback from residents about improvements at both Glenwood and Windsor pools. These are the first pools to be identified for improvements. The online public meeting for Glenwood and Windsor pools will be held on Thursday, May 13, from 6-8 p.m. We want to hear from you! Pre-register for this meeting.

The results of the survey and public meetings will be used to develop a comprehensive plan for aquatics that will provide opportunities for community gathering places, enjoying outdoor recreation and developing skills for healthy lifestyles.  

Our department will hold public meetings about the rest of our aquatics facilities throughout the rest of this year so stay tuned for more updates.

Learn more about the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan by visiting www.columbusaquatics.org.
